name: Passkey Sign-In
summary: A returning user identifies the account by email, chooses passkey authentication, completes the platform passkey ceremony, and reaches the application home view.
finalOutcome: The email-resolved durable user has an authenticated session established through a valid user-verified passkey assertion.

sourceReferences.note: The user-bound passkey manager owns challenge validation, credential ownership checks, WebAuthn assertion verification, user verification policy, and signature-counter advancement.

Passkey Sign In resolves the entered email to the expected durable UserId and delegates to the same user-bound passkey proof primitive used by MFA, while primary completion does not mutate MFA freshness.
The server exposes email-bound begin, browser-session complete, and mobile-token complete operations and establishes application state only after the proof service returns a durable user.
Angular retains normalized email and routes action:continue-passkey to the canonical Passkey surface without a server call.
Angular uses the retained email with the email-bound passkey operations and the browser WebAuthn ceremony.
React Native retains normalized email in AuthFlow and routes the Passkey choice without a server call.
React Native performs the native passkey ceremony and completes the email-bound proof into the existing token-session lifecycle.
Generated AuthClient contracts expose typed email-bound passkey begin, browser complete, and mobile token complete methods.
Service proof covers normalized email resolution, neutral account/passkey availability failures, exact-user completion and rejected assertions.
Real-manager proof covers UV-required challenge creation, per-user allowCredentials, challenge/credential ownership, signature counter advancement, and no primary-auth MFA freshness mutation.
Common adapter proof covers durable proven-user browser session and mobile token completion and rejects missing proof before mutation.

Direct Passkey-first discovery is deferred from launch scope. Email-first primary Passkey and Password-then-Passkey MFA share one user-bound passkey proof primitive; the surrounding authentication state determines how successful proof is consumed.
Both canonical primary Passkey scenarios now have complete authored test obligations. Runtime C# and UI execution evidence remain separate from authored Tests status.
